first_impression: A warm stone-courtyard gardening portrait. An open broad spiral spring, crafted brass assembly, raised terracotta reservoir and copper water route make the practical clockwork premise readable. Face and bob visibly follow the reference.

gates.evidence: Open spiral barrel and center arbor at left are clear; the arbor-to-pinion-to-broad-wheel tooth engagement cannot be followed as the complete named route.
A circular side disk, bars and valve are present, but no simultaneously readable raised cam nose, follower/lever pivot and opposite-end valve-stem contact.
Raised reservoir, continuous copper tube, valve, outlet and thin water stream are visible. Leaves obscure the soil landing; a distinct darker landing patch cannot be confirmed.
Both arms/hands are plausible. The left hand rests among soil/plants near the tray edge rather than on a clearly readable wooden rim; the exact right-hand/key interface is partly hidden.
Downward attention links readable face, foreground mechanism and watered seedling area within limestone/timber/terracotta courtyard context.
Jaw-length dark bob, separated fringe, softly tapered face and natural lip form visibly follow the supplied portrait; no identity claim.

per_card_scope: A01 spring/barrel/arbor depiction is visible locally; this is not qualification of every A01 gate or of all Clockpunk cards.
